summary: Deliver queryable SIEM-ready audit slab with UTC-anchored checksums and selective redaction
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests an on-demand export that is both human-auditable and directly ingestible by their SIEM. They want the following delivered as one package: a set of time-ordered, queryable Parquet shards; a manifest of UTC-anchored checksums per shard; per-tenant HMAC proof for integrity; a compact redaction map that documents which fields were pseudonymized; and a lightweight index to allow resume tokens for partial replay.

Impact:
Aurora Bank needs this bundle to complete a quarterly internal audit and to satisfy a regulator request. They cannot proceed with regulatory sign-off until the export includes deterministic UTC timestamps, a tamper-evident manifest, and a documented redaction policy. The current ad-hoc exports don't meet their legal team's requirements.

Requested deliverable (customer asks):
1) Parquet shards partitioned by hour, canonicalized to UTC, compressed with snappy, with a lightweight index file per shard.
2) Manifest file (JSON-LD) listing shard names, row counts, UTC min/max, SHA256 checksums, and a per-shard HMAC using a customer-provided key-encryption envelope.
3) Redaction map: CSV that lists original field names, redaction method (hash/pseudonymize/strip), salt identifier, and a reversible/pseudonymization note (if reversible, include KMS-key reference).
4) Resume token format and a short README explaining how to replay a partial window to resume ingestion into their SIEM.
5) One example query and a sample of the exported rows (first 200 rows) with redaction applied.

Notes on uniqueness/constraints from customer:
- Time normalization must be to UTC with explicit timezone tag per-record.
- Pseudonymization should be deterministic across export runs (same salt) but reversible only with KMS unwrap.
- They prefer per-shard HMAC so they can validate delivery without fetching full bundles.
- Wants check that export ordering is monotonic by UTC timestamp within each shard.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requested ad-hoc export via support form on 2026-03-13.
2) Support validated entitlement and escalation path; requested the security questionnaire and KMS public key for HMAC envelope.
3) Attempted to generate a proof-of-concept export using existing export job with 'tz-normalize' flag enabled; noticed timestamp collisions around DST edges in customer's event stream.
4) Observed missing index files in the last automated export; index generator job crashed on a row with deeply nested JSON field.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-14 10:15 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed regulatory requirements include per-shard tamper evidence and deterministic pseudonymization. Requested KMS key usage policy and preferred manifest schema from customer.
2026-03-14 11:02 - Eng (Diego): Reproduced indexer crash locally with sample event containing null-keyed map. Hypothesis: our flattener assumes string keys; needs guard for non-string keys.

2026-03-14 12:30 - SRE (Maya): Verified export pipeline can emit UTC-tagged timestamps; however, the earlier job used local-tz fallback for records with missing tz - we should normalize those to UTC and mark as 'inferred' in the index.

2026-03-14 13:10 - Support (Aisha): Obtained customer KMS public key material (key-id: aurora-kms-01) and confirmation they accept per-shard HMAC prevented without sharing KEK. Started drafting manifest schema that includes hmac_algorithm and key_id metadata.
2026-03-14 14:05 - Eng (Diego): Small patch proposed to indexer to skip/emit placeholder for unsupported nested map keys; PR linked below. Need security review for HMAC implementation.
comments: 2026-03-14 10:25 - Aisha (Support): @Aurora Bank thanks for the details. We're scoping a one-off export and will run it in a test bucket first. Please confirm the rotation window for the salt and whether you require an audit trail tying the salt to a ticket number.
2026-03-14 11:20 - Aurora Bank (Customer): We need the salt tied to this ticket; rotation only after regulator sign-off. KMS key can be used to unwrap during replay in our environment.
2026-03-14 12:45 - Diego (Eng): Uploaded a minimal PR to handle non-string map keys in indexer: github.com/redwood-inference/exporter/pull/58. Marking for security review @sec-team.
2026-03-14 14:30 - Maya (SRE): I can run a dry-run export to the customer's test bucket once the indexer fix is merged; will schedule maintenance window to avoid coinciding with heavy ingestion.
resolution_notes: Pending: Merge indexer fix and complete security review of HMAC envelope. Plan: 1) merge exporter PR, 2) produce dry-run to customer's test bucket, 3) provide packaged zip with Parquet shards, manifest.jsonld, redaction-map.csv, resume-index.json, and README. Estimate delivery in 3 business days once PR merges.
customer_confirmation_needed: Confirm salt rotation policy (tied to SUP-213377 or rotated after regulator sign-off)
Confirm whether reversible pseudonymization is allowed (we will need KMS unwrap permissions)
Confirm target S3 bucket name and account for transfer (or provide temporary presigned upload location)
audit_requirements_summary: UTC-canonical timestamps, per-shard SHA256 and per-shard HMAC (customer KEK), deterministic pseudonymization with KMS-encrypted salt reference, resume tokens for partial replay, and a human-readable redaction map.
estimated_workflow_steps: Security review of HMAC envelope and manifest schema (sec-team)
Merge exporter/indexer patch and deploy to staging (eng)
Dry-run export to customer test bucket and validation with customer's SOC analyst (sre + support)
Produce final evidence bundle and upload to customer-designated storage (support)
Capture transfer receipts and provide manifest validation instructions (support)
